sanskrit: nātaḥ śrīmattaraṃ kiṃ cid anyat pathyatamaṃ tathā prabhaviṣṇor yathā tāta kṣamā sarvatra sarvadā
english: There is nothing more auspicious than this, nothing more beneficial for one who seeks prosperity: O dear one, forbearance everywhere and always.

sanskrit: kṣamed aśaktaḥ sarvasya śaktimān dharmakāraṇāt arthānarthau samau yasya tasya nityaṃ kṣamā hitā
english: The powerless man forgives everything out of weakness; the powerful man forgives for the sake of dharma. For one to whom gain and loss are equal, forbearance is always beneficial.

sanskrit: yat sukhaṃ sevamāno 'pi dharmārthābhyāṃ na hīyate kāmaṃ tad upaseveta na mūḍhavratam ācaret
english: Whatever pleasure one pursues without thereby falling away from dharma and artha — that desire one may indulge; one should not practice the vow of a fool.

sanskrit: duḥkhārteṣu pramatteṣu nāstikeṣv alaseṣu ca na śrīr vasaty adānteṣu ye cotsāhavivarjitāḥ
english: Prosperity does not dwell among those afflicted by sorrow, those who are heedless, those who deny the next world, the idle, the unrestrained, and those devoid of enterprise.

sanskrit: ārjavena naraṃ yuktam ārjavāt savyapatrapam aśaktimantaṃ manyanto dharṣayanti kubuddhayaḥ
english: Those of wicked intellect, taking a man endowed with straightforwardness for a weakling — ashamed of his very straightforwardness — presume to affront him.

sanskrit: atyāryam atidātāram atiśūram ativratam prajñābhimāninaṃ caiva śrīr bhayān nopasarpati
english: Prosperity does not approach, out of fear, one who is exceedingly noble, exceedingly generous, exceedingly heroic, excessively given to vows, or one who is arrogant of his own wisdom.

sanskrit: agnihotraphalā vedāḥ śīlavṛttaphalaṃ śrutam ratiputraphalā dārā dattabhuktaphalaṃ dhanam
english: The Vedas bear fruit in the agnihotra sacrifice; learning bears fruit in good conduct and practice; a wife bears fruit in love and offspring; wealth bears its fruit in giving and enjoyment.

sanskrit: adharmopārjitair arthair yaḥ karoty aurdhvadehikam na sa tasya phalaṃ pretya bhuṅkte 'rthasya durāgamāt
english: He who performs funeral rites with wealth unrighteously acquired does not enjoy the fruit of that wealth after death, because the means of acquisition was wrong.

sanskrit: kāntāravanadurgeṣu kṛcchrāsv āpatsu saṃbhrame udyateṣu ca śastreṣu nāsti śeṣavatāṃ bhayam
english: In impassable forests and wildernesses, in severe calamities and turmoil, and even when weapons are raised — those who have a remainder of merit know no fear.

sanskrit: utthānaṃ saṃyamo dākṣyam apramādo dhṛtiḥ smṛtiḥ samīkṣya ca samārambho viddhi mūlaṃ bhavasya tat
english: Effort, self-restraint, skill, heedfulness, firmness, memory, and undertaking after deliberation — know these to be the root of prosperity.

sanskrit: tapo balaṃ tāpasānāṃ brahma brahmavidāṃ balam hiṃsā balam asādhūnāṃ kṣamā guṇavatāṃ balam
english: Austerity is the strength of ascetics; Brahman-knowledge is the strength of those who know Brahman; violence is the strength of the wicked; forbearance is the strength of the virtuous.

sanskrit: aṣṭau tāny avrataghnāni āpo mūlaṃ phalaṃ payaḥ havir brāhmaṇakāmyā ca guror vacanam auṣadham
english: These eight do not break a vow: water, roots, fruit, milk, oblation, the wish of a brahmin, the word of a teacher, and medicine.

sanskrit: na tatparasya saṃdadhyāt pratikūlaṃ yadātmanaḥ saṃgraheṇaiṣa dharmaḥ syāt kāmād anyaḥ pravartate
english: One should not impose on another what is disagreeable to oneself — this in brief is the essence of dharma; all other conduct proceeds from desire.

sanskrit: akrodhena jayet krodham asādhuṃ sādhunā jayet jayet kadaryaṃ dānena jayet satyena cānṛtam
english: Conquer anger by the absence of anger; conquer the unrighteous man by righteousness; conquer the miser by generosity; conquer falsehood by truth.

sanskrit: strīdhūrtake 'lase bhīrau caṇḍe puruṣamānini caure kṛtaghne viśvāso na kāryo na ca nāstike
english: One should never place trust in a woman who is a cheat, in the lazy, in the coward, in the violent, in one who fancies himself a great man, in a thief, in an ungrateful person, or in a nihilist.

sanskrit: abhivādanaśīlasya nityaṃ vṛddhopasevinaḥ catvāri saṃpravardhante kīrtir āyur yaśobalam
english: For one who is habitually respectful and who always serves elders, four things increase: fame, lifespan, glory, and strength.

sanskrit: atikleśena ye 'rthāḥ syur dharmasyātikrameṇa ca arer vā praṇipātena mā sma teṣu manaḥ kṛthāḥ
english: Do not set your mind on wealth that comes through excessive suffering, through transgression of dharma, or through supplication of an enemy.

sanskrit: avidyaḥ puruṣaḥ śocyaḥ śocyaṃ mithunam aprajam nirāhārāḥ prajāḥ śocyāḥ śocyaṃ rāṣṭram arājakam
english: An unlearned man is pitiable; a childless couple is pitiable; subjects without food are pitiable; a kingdom without a king is pitiable.

sanskrit: adhvā jarā dehavatāṃ parvatānāṃ jalaṃ jarā asaṃbhogo jarā strīṇāṃ vākśalyaṃ manaso jarā
english: The road is the old age of those with bodies; water is the old age of mountains; lack of union is the old age of women; a sharp word is the old age of the mind.

sanskrit: anāmnāyamalā vedā brāhmaṇasyāvrataṃ malam kautūhalamalā sādhvī vipravāsamalāḥ striyaḥ
english: The Vedas are tainted by lack of recitation; a brahmin is tainted by lack of observance of vows; a virtuous woman is tainted by curiosity; women are tainted by prolonged separation from their husbands.

sanskrit: suvarṇasya malaṃ rūpyaṃ rūpyasyāpi malaṃ trapu jñeyaṃ trapumalaṃ sīsaṃ sīsasyāpi malaṃ malam
english: Silver is the dross of gold; tin is the dross of silver; lead is known as the dross of tin; and dross itself is the dross of lead.

sanskrit: na svapnena jayen nidrāṃ na kāmena striyaṃ jayet nendhanena jayed agniṃ na pānena surāṃ jayet
english: One does not conquer sleep by sleeping; one does not conquer a woman by desire; one does not conquer fire by adding fuel; one does not conquer liquor by drinking it.

sanskrit: yasya dānajitaṃ mitram amitrā yudhi nirjitāḥ annapānajitā dārāḥ saphalaṃ tasya jīvitam
english: He whose friends are won by generosity, whose enemies are conquered in battle, and whose wife is won by food and drink — his life bears full fruit.

sanskrit: sahasriṇo 'pi jīvanti jīvanti śatinas tathā dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ vimuñcecchāṃ na kathaṃ cin na jīvyate
english: Even those who possess thousands live; even those who possess hundreds live. O Dhṛtarāṣṭra, give up desire; there is no way one cannot live.

sanskrit: yat pṛthivyāṃ vrīhiyavaṃ hiraṇyaṃ paśavaḥ striyaḥ nālam ekasya tat sarvam iti paśyan na muhyati
english: Whatever rice and barley, gold, cattle, and women there are on this earth — all that is not enough for one person alone. Seeing this truth, one is not deluded.

sanskrit: rājan bhūyo bravīmi tvāṃ putreṣu samam ācara samatā yadi te rājan sveṣu pāṇḍusuteṣu ca
english: O king, I say to you again: act equally toward your sons. O king, let there be equity between your own sons and the sons of Pāṇḍu.

sanskrit: vidura uvāca yo 'bhyarthitaḥ sadbhir asajjamānaḥ; karoty arthaṃ śaktim ahāpayitvā kṣipraṃ yaśas taṃ samupaiti santam alaṃ; prasannā hi sukhāya santaḥ
english: Vidura said: He who, when requested by good men, without hesitation accomplishes the task without diminishing his capacity — glory quickly comes to that virtuous man. For when good men are pleased, it leads to happiness.

sanskrit: mahāntam apy artham adharmayuktaṃ; yaḥ saṃtyajaty anupākruṣṭa eva sukhaṃ sa duḥkhāny avamucya śete; jīrṇāṃ tvacaṃ sarpa ivāvamucya
english: He who, of his own accord without being reproached, relinquishes even great wealth tainted with unrighteousness — he sleeps happily, freed from sorrows, like a serpent that has shed its old skin.

sanskrit: anṛtaṃ ca samutkarṣe rājagāmi ca paiśunam guroś cālīkanirbandhaḥ samāni brahmahatyayā
english: Falsehood in self-aggrandizement, tale-bearing that reaches the king's ears, and persistent false accusation of one's teacher — these are equal to the slaying of a brahmin.

sanskrit: asūyaikapadaṃ mṛtyur ativādaḥ śriyo vadhaḥ aśuśrūṣā tvarā ślāghā vidyāyāḥ śatravas trayaḥ
english: Envy is death in a single step; harsh speech is the slayer of prosperity. Disobedience, haste, and boastfulness are the three enemies of learning.

sanskrit: sukhārthinaḥ kuto vidyā nāsti vidyārthinaḥ sukham sukhārthī vā tyajed vidyāṃ vidyārthī vā sukhaṃ tyajet
english: Where is knowledge for one who seeks comfort? There is no comfort for one who seeks knowledge. The seeker of comfort must abandon knowledge, or the seeker of knowledge must abandon comfort.

sanskrit: nāgnis tṛpyati kāṣṭhānāṃ nāpagānāṃ mahodadhiḥ nāntakaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ na puṃsāṃ vāmalocanā
english: Fire is not satiated by fuel; the great ocean is not satiated by rivers; Death is not satiated by all creatures; nor is a fair-eyed woman satiated by men.

sanskrit: āśā dhṛtiṃ hanti samṛddhim antakaḥ; krodhaḥ śriyaṃ hanti yaśaḥ kadaryatā apālanaṃ hanti paśūṃś ca rājann; ekaḥ kruddho brāhmaṇo hanti rāṣṭram
english: Hope destroys steadfastness; Death destroys prosperity; anger destroys glory; miserliness destroys fame. Neglect destroys cattle, O king; and a single enraged brahmin destroys a kingdom.

sanskrit: ajaś ca kāṃsyaṃ ca rathaś ca nityaṃ; madhv ākarṣaḥ śakuniḥ śrotriyaś ca vṛddho jñātir avasanno vayasya; etāni te santu gṛhe sadaiva
english: A goat, a bronze vessel, a chariot always ready, a honey-drawing bee, a learned brahmin, an elder kinsman fallen on hard times, and a friend — may these always be in your house.

sanskrit: ajokṣā candanaṃ vīṇā ādarśo madhusarpiṣī viṣam audumbaraṃ śaṅkhaḥ svarṇaṃ nābhiś ca rocanā
english: A she-goat, sandalwood, a lute, a mirror, honey and ghee, poison, an udumbara fruit, a conch shell, gold, a navel piece, and yellow pigment —

sanskrit: gṛhe sthāpayitavyāni dhanyāni manur abravīt devabrāhmaṇapūjārtham atithīnāṃ ca bhārata
english: — these auspicious items ought to be kept in the house, said Manu, O Bhārata, for the worship of gods and brahmins, and for the reception of guests.

sanskrit: idaṃ ca tvāṃ sarvaparaṃ bravīmi; puṇyaṃ padaṃ tāta mahāviśiṣṭam na jātu kāmān na bhayān na lobhād; dharmaṃ tyajej jīvitasyāpi hetoḥ
english: And this supreme counsel I declare to you, the most meritorious and distinguished of teachings, O dear one: Never abandon dharma — not for desire, not for fear, not for greed, not even for the sake of your own life.

sanskrit: nityo dharmaḥ sukhaduḥkhe tv anitye; nityo jīvo dhātur asya tv anityaḥ tyaktvānityaṃ pratitiṣṭhasva nitye; saṃtuṣya tvaṃ toṣaparo hi lābhaḥ
english: Dharma is eternal; pleasure and pain are transient. The self is eternal; the body that sustains it is transient. Abandoning the transient, be established in the eternal. Be content — for contentment is the highest gain.

sanskrit: mahābalān paśya mahānubhāvān; praśāsya bhūmiṃ dhanadhānyapūrṇām rājyāni hitvā vipulāṃś ca bhogān; gatān narendrān vaśam antakasya
english: Behold those mighty and illustrious men — having ruled the earth full of wealth and grain, having abandoned kingdoms and vast enjoyments — those kings have gone into the power of Death.

sanskrit: mṛtaṃ putraṃ duḥkhapuṣṭaṃ manuṣyā; utkṣipya rājan svagṛhān nirharanti taṃ muktakeśāḥ karuṇaṃ rudantaś; citāmadhye kāṣṭham iva kṣipanti
english: Men lift a dead son — one nourished with such sorrow — and carry him out of their own homes, O king; with hair disheveled and crying piteously, they cast him into the midst of the pyre like a log of wood.

sanskrit: anyo dhanaṃ pretagatasya bhuṅkte; vayāṃsi cāgniś ca śarīradhātūn dvābhyām ayaṃ saha gacchaty amutra; puṇyena pāpena ca veṣṭyamānaḥ
english: Another enjoys the wealth of one who has gone to the realm of the dead; birds and fire consume the elements of his body. He departs to the other world with only two companions — merit and sin — wrapped around him.

sanskrit: utsṛjya vinivartante jñātayaḥ suhṛdaḥ sutāḥ agnau prāstaṃ tu puruṣaṃ karmānveti svayaṃkṛtam
english: Kinsmen, friends, and sons turn back after abandoning him; but the man who has been cast into the fire — his own deeds follow him.

sanskrit: asmāl lokād ūrdhvam amuṣya cādho; mahat tamas tiṣṭhati hy andhakāram tad vai mahāmohanam indriyāṇāṃ; budhyasva mā tvāṃ pralabheta rājan
english: Above this world and below that other world a great darkness stands — a blinding gloom. That is the great delusion of the senses. Awaken, O king — let it not deceive you.

sanskrit: idaṃ vacaḥ śakṣyasi ced yathāvan; niśamya sarvaṃ pratipattum evam yaśaḥ paraṃ prāpsyasi jīvaloke; bhayaṃ na cāmutra na ceha te 'sti
english: If you are able to hear all this counsel and act accordingly, you will attain supreme glory in the world of the living; and there will be no fear for you in the next world, nor in this one.

sanskrit: ātmā nadī bhārata puṇyatīrthā; satyodakā dhṛtikūlā damormiḥ tasyāṃ snātaḥ pūyate puṇyakarmā; puṇyo hy ātmā nityam ambho 'mbha eva
english: The self is a river of sacred fords, O Bhārata — its waters are truth, its banks are fortitude, its waves are self-restraint. One who bathes in it, performing virtuous deeds, is purified. For the self is always holy water itself.

sanskrit: kāmakrodhagrāhavatīṃ pañcendriyajalāṃ nadīm kṛtvā dhṛtimayīṃ nāvaṃ janmadurgāṇi saṃtara
english: Making a boat of steadfastness, cross the river whose waters are the five senses and whose crocodiles are desire and anger — cross the difficult straits of rebirth.

sanskrit: prajñāvṛddhaṃ dharmavṛddhaṃ svabandhuṃ; vidyāvṛddhaṃ vayasā cāpi vṛddham kāryākārye pūjayitvā prasādya; yaḥ saṃpṛcchen na sa muhyet kadā cit
english: He who, honouring and propitiating one who is great in wisdom, great in dharma, a kinsman, great in learning, and also great in years — who consults such a one in matters of what should and should not be done — such a person will never be deluded.

sanskrit: dhṛtyā śiśnodaraṃ rakṣet pāṇipādaṃ ca cakṣuṣā cakṣuḥśrotre ca manasā mano vācaṃ ca karmaṇā
english: By steadfastness guard the loins and belly; by the eyes guard the hands and feet; guard the eyes and ears by the mind; and guard the mind by action.

sanskrit: nityodakī nityayajñopavītī; nityasvādhyāyī patitānnavarjī ṛtaṃ bruvan gurave karma kurvan; na brāhmaṇaś cyavate brahmalokāt
english: One who always performs the water-rite, always wears the sacred thread, always studies the scriptures, avoids the food of the fallen, speaks the truth, and performs his duty to his teacher — such a brahmin never falls from the world of Brahman.

sanskrit: adhītya vedān parisaṃstīrya cāgnīn; iṣṭvā yajñaiḥ pālayitvā prajāś ca gobrāhmaṇārthe śastrapūtāntarātmā; hataḥ saṃgrāme kṣatriyaḥ svargam eti
english: A kshatriya who has studied the Vedas, tended the sacred fires, performed sacrifices, protected his subjects, whose inner self is purified by the sword for the sake of cows and brahmins, and who is slain in battle — he goes to heaven.

sanskrit: vaiśyo 'dhītya brāhmaṇān kṣatriyāṃś ca; dhanaiḥ kāle saṃvibhajyāśritāṃś ca tretāpūtaṃ dhūmam āghrāya puṇyaṃ; pretya svarge devasukhāni bhuṅkte
english: A vaishya who has studied the brahmins and kshatriyas, who in due season shares his wealth with his dependants, who inhales the auspicious smoke purified by the Tretā sacrifice — after death he enjoys the pleasures of heaven among the gods.

sanskrit: brahmakṣatraṃ vaiśyavarṇaṃ ca śūdraḥ; krameṇaitān nyāyataḥ pūjayānaḥ tuṣṭeṣv eteṣv avyatho dagdhapāpas; tyaktvā dehaṃ svargasukhāni bhuṅkte
english: A shudra who duly and in proper order honours the brahmin, kshatriya, and vaishya varnas — when these are pleased, he, untroubled and with his sins burned away, abandons the body and enjoys the pleasures of heaven.

sanskrit: cāturvarṇyasyaiṣa dharmas tavokto; hetuṃ cātra bruvato me nibodha kṣātrād dharmād dhīyate pāṇḍuputras; taṃ tvaṃ rājan rājadharme niyuṅkṣva
english: This dharma of the four varnas has been declared to you. Now hear the reason I am telling you this: the son of Pāṇḍu is being deprived of his kshatriya dharma. O king, engage him in the duty of a king.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca evam etad yathā māṃ tvam anuśāsasi nityadā mamāpi ca matiḥ saumya bhavaty evaṃ yathāttha mām
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: It is indeed as you always instruct me, O gentle one; my own mind too becomes thus, even as you say to me.

sanskrit: sā tu buddhiḥ kṛtāpy evaṃ pāṇḍavān prati me sadā duryodhanaṃ samāsādya punar viparivartate
english: But that resolve, though formed in this way, always turns around when it meets with Duryodhana in regard to the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: na diṣṭam abhyatikrāntuṃ śakyaṃ martyena kena cit diṣṭam eva kṛtaṃ manye pauruṣaṃ tu nirarthakam
english: No mortal is able to transcend what is fated. I consider that only fate acts; human effort is without purpose.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca anuktaṃ yadi te kiṃ cid vācā vidura vidyate tan me śuśrūṣave brūhi vicitrāṇi hi bhāṣase
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: If there is anything, O Vidura, that you have left unsaid, tell me who am eager to hear. You speak of many wondrous things.

sanskrit: vidura uvāca dhṛtarāṣṭra kumāro vai yaḥ purāṇaḥ sanātanaḥ sanatsujātaḥ provāca mṛtyur nāstīti bhārata
english: Vidura said: O Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the ancient and eternal youth Sanatsujāta declared, O Bhārata, that there is no death.

sanskrit: sa te guhyān prakāśāṃś ca sarvān hṛdayasaṃśrayān pravakṣyati mahārāja sarvabuddhimatāṃ varaḥ
english: He, the foremost among all the wise, will expound to you all the secret and the manifest teachings that reside in the heart, O great king.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca kiṃ tvaṃ na veda tad bhūyo yan me brūyāt sanātanaḥ tvam eva vidura brūhi prajñāśeṣo 'sti cet tava
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: Is there anything more that the eternal one would tell me that you yourself do not know? You yourself speak, O Vidura, if there is any remainder of wisdom in you.

sanskrit: vidura uvāca śūdrayonāv ahaṃ jāto nāto 'nyad vaktum utsahe kumārasya tu yā buddhir veda tāṃ śāśvatīm aham
english: Vidura said: I am born of a shudra womb and therefore dare not say more than this. But I know the eternal wisdom that is the understanding of that youth.

sanskrit: brāhmīṃ hi yonim āpannaḥ suguhyam api yo vadet na tena garhyo devānāṃ tasmād etad bravīmi te
english: For one born into a brahmin womb, even speaking what is most secret — he is not censured by the gods for that. Therefore I tell you this much.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca bravīhi vidura tvaṃ me purāṇaṃ taṃ sanātanam katham etena dehena syād ihaiva samāgamaḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: Tell me, O Vidura, of that ancient and eternal one. How can a meeting with him happen right here through this body?

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca cintayām āsa viduras tam ṛṣiṃ saṃśitavratam sa ca tac cintitaṃ jñātvā darśayām āsa bhārata
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Vidura meditated upon that sage of sharpened vows; and that sage, knowing he had been thought of, revealed himself, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: sa cainaṃ pratijagrāha vidhidṛṣṭena karmaṇā sukhopaviṣṭaṃ viśrāntam athainaṃ viduro 'bravīt
english: Vidura received him with the rites prescribed by the scriptures. When the sage was comfortably seated and rested, Vidura spoke to him.

sanskrit: bhagavan saṃśayaḥ kaś cid dhṛtarāṣṭrasya mānase yo na śakyo mayā vaktuṃ tam asmai vaktum arhasi yaṃ śrutvāyaṃ manuṣyendraḥ sukhaduḥkhātigo bhavet
english: O blessed one, there is a certain doubt in the mind of Dhṛtarāṣṭra which I am not able to resolve. Please speak to him of it — hearing which, this lord of men may transcend pleasure and pain.

sanskrit: lābhālābhau priyadveṣyau yathainaṃ na jarāntakau viṣaheran bhayāmarṣau kṣutpipāse madodbhavau aratiś caiva tandrī ca kāmakrodhau kṣayodayau
english: Speak so that gain and loss, the dear and the hateful, old age and death, fear and anger, hunger and thirst born of intoxication, discontent and sloth, desire and anger, decline and rise — may not torment him.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato rājā dhṛtarāṣṭro manīṣī; saṃpūjya vākyaṃ vidureritaṃ tat sanatsujātaṃ rahite mahātmā; papraccha buddhiṃ paramāṃ bubhūṣan
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then the wise king Dhṛtarāṣṭra, that great soul, having honoured the words spoken by Vidura, questioned Sanatsujāta in private, desiring the highest wisdom.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca sanatsujāta yadīdaṃ śṛṇomi; mṛtyur hi nāstīti tavopadeśam devāsurā hy ācaran brahmacaryam; amṛtyave tat kataran nu satyam
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: O Sanatsujāta, I have heard this teaching of yours — that there is no death. And yet gods and asuras both practised brahmacharya for the sake of immortality. Which of these is truly true?

sanskrit: sanatsujāta uvāca amṛtyuḥ karmaṇā ke cin mṛtyur nāstīti cāpare śṛṇu me bruvato rājan yathaitan mā viśaṅkithāḥ
english: Sanatsujāta said: Some say that through ritual action one attains immortality; others say that there is no death. O king, listen as I explain this — do not doubt it.

sanskrit: ubhe satye kṣatriyādyapravṛtte; moho mṛtyuḥ saṃmato yaḥ kavīnām pramādaṃ vai mṛtyum ahaṃ bravīmi; sadāpramādam amṛtatvaṃ bravīmi
english: Both are true, set in motion from the time of kshatriyas and others. Delusion is what the wise consider to be death. I declare heedlessness to be death; I declare constant vigilance to be immortality.

sanskrit: pramādād vai asurāḥ parābhavann; apramādād brahmabhūtā bhavanti na vai mṛtyur vyāghra ivātti jantūn; na hy asya rūpam upalabhyate ha
english: Through heedlessness indeed the asuras were defeated; through heedlessness men become Brahman. Death does not devour beings like a tiger; for its form cannot be perceived.

sanskrit: yamaṃ tv eke mṛtyum ato 'nyam āhur; ātmāvasannam amṛtaṃ brahmacaryam pitṛloke rājyam anuśāsti devaḥ; śivaḥ śivānām aśivo 'śivānām
english: Some call Yama death, others call it something else. Immortality rests in the self; brahmacharya is immortality. That god rules the kingdom in the realm of the ancestors — auspicious to the auspicious, inauspicious to the inauspicious.

sanskrit: āsyād eṣa niḥsarate narāṇāṃ; krodhaḥ pramādo moharūpaś ca mṛtyuḥ te mohitās tadvaśe vartamānā; itaḥ pretās tatra punaḥ patanti
english: From the mouth of men this issues forth: anger, heedlessness, and delusion — these are death's very form. Deluded, moving under its sway, the dead fall from here and fall there again.

sanskrit: tatas taṃ devā anu viplavante; ato mṛtyur maraṇākhyām upaiti karmodaye karmaphalānurāgās; tatrānu yānti na taranti mṛtyum
english: Then the gods too are swept along by it; hence death comes to bear the name of dying. Those attached to the fruits of action at the arising of action — they follow along there and do not cross over death.

sanskrit: yo 'bhidhyāyann utpatiṣṇūn nihanyād; anādareṇāpratibudhyamānaḥ sa vai mṛtyur mṛtyur ivātti bhūtvā; evaṃ vidvān yo vinihanti kāmān
english: He who, while brooding, would strike down the impulses that arise — he who, through disregard, remains unawakened — he becomes death itself, consuming like death. Such is the one who, knowing, destroys desires.

sanskrit: kāmānusārī puruṣaḥ kāmān anu vinaśyati kāmān vyudasya dhunute yat kiṃ cit puruṣo rajaḥ
english: A man who follows after desires is destroyed along with those desires. He who casts off desires shakes off whatever dust of rajas remains in him.

sanskrit: tamo 'prakāśo bhūtānāṃ narako 'yaṃ pradṛśyate gṛhyanta iva dhāvanti gacchantaḥ śvabhram unmukhāḥ
english: This is the hell of beings — darkness without light — that is seen ahead. They rush forward as if being seized, heading face-first into the pit.

sanskrit: abhidhyā vai prathamaṃ hanti cainaṃ; kāmakrodhau gṛhya cainaṃ tu paścāt ete bālān mṛtyave prāpayanti; dhīrās tu dhairyeṇa taranti mṛtyum
english: Covetousness first slays a man; then desire and anger seize him afterward. These bring the foolish to death. But the wise cross over death by their steadfastness.

sanskrit: amanyamānaḥ kṣatriya kiṃ cid anyan; nādhīyate tārṇa ivāsya vyāghraḥ krodhāl lobhān mohamayāntarātmā; sa vai mṛtyus tvac charīre ya eṣaḥ
english: Not thinking of anything other than himself, O kshatriya, one does not study — like a tiger among blades of grass. That one whose inner self is made of anger, greed, and delusion — that very one dwelling in your body is death.
